Advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) are generating excitement worldwide. Better healthcare, more effective research and education, and improved productivity are just some of the anticipated benefits. Around the world, billions of dollars are being invested in AI by both governments and the private sector. Global competition to build the fastest computers and the most sophisticated AI systems is on the rise. While these developments are undoubtedly promising, they come with an uncomfortable [...] Artificial Intelligence may resolve global challenges. However, the field can only provide so much. A society's goals must determine the direction of human affairs and science. Aiming too high in our quest for digital intelligence may deplete essential resources, disrupt natural ecosystems, or neglect the needs and/or desires of local communities. Eventually, societies must consider whether the costs for such goals are worth the outcome. [...] Although we must develop sophisticated, cleaner, more effective technologies, our goal should be to preserve and improve the natural world. Thus, if there are trade-offs, it is better to sacrifice technology than to sacrifice ecosystems. The future of AI cannot be at the cost of the natural world.

items.summary:
Learning to reason with LLMs \| OpenAI

September 12, 2024

[Release](https://openai.com/research/index/release/)

# Learning to reason with LLMs

We are introducing OpenAI o1, a new large language model trained with reinforcement learning to perform complex reasoning. o1 thinks before it answers—it can produce a long internal chain of thought before responding to the user.

[Contributions](https://openai.com/openai-o1-contributions/) [Try ChatGPT(opens in a new window)](https://chatgpt.com/?openaicom-did=ace47a51-46de-4d9c-a6a5-e7819b768e45&openaicom_referred=true)

## This post introduced OpenAI o1.

The ChatGPT access information reflects the September 2024 launch. o1‑preview and o1‑mini have been retired from the API; o1 is deprecated. See the [API deprecation schedule⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations).

For the current experience:

[View current API models(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)

[Try ChatGPT(opens in a new window)](https://chatgpt.com/?openaicom-did=ace47a51-46de-4d9c-a6a5-e7819b768e45&openaicom_referred=true)

Listen to article8:58

OpenAI o1 ranks in the 89th percentile on competitive programming questions (Codeforces), places among the top 500 students in the US in a qualifier for the USA Math Olympiad (AIME), and exceeds human PhD-level accuracy on a benchmark of physics, biology, and chemistry problems (GPQA). While the work needed to make this new model as easy to use as current models is still ongoing, we are releasing an early version of this model, OpenAI o1‑preview, for immediate use in ChatGPT and to [trusted API users⁠(opens in a new window)](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/rate-limits/usage-tiers).

Our large-scale reinforcement learning algorithm teaches the model how to think productively using its chain of thought in a highly data-efficient training process. We have found that the performance of o1 consistently improves with more reinforcement learning (train-time compute) and with more time spent thinking (test-time compute). The constraints on scaling this approach differ substantially from those of LLM pretraining, and we are continuing to investigate them.

![The image shows two scatter plots comparing "o1 AIME accuracy" during training and at test time. Both charts have "pass@1 accuracy" on the y-axis and compute (log scale) on the x-axis. The dots indicate increasing accuracy with more compute time.](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/3OO9wpK8pjcdemjd7g50xk/5ec2cc9d11f008cd754e8cefbc1c99f5/compute.png?w=3840&q=90&fm=webp)

o1 performance smoothly improves with both train-time and test-time compute

## Evals

To highlight the reasoning improvement over GPT‑4o, we tested our models on a diverse set of human exams and ML benchmarks. We show that o1 significantly outperforms GPT‑4o on the vast majority of these reasoning-heavy tasks. Unless otherwise specified, we evaluated o1 on the maximal test-time compute setting.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

args.text:
Dưới đây là hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng:
n = 10
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n} là: {fibonacci(n)}")
```

### Giải thích:
- **Trường hợp cơ sở (Base case):** Nếu `n <= 0` trả về 0, nếu `n == 1` trả về 1.
- **Bước đệ quy (Recursive step):** Tính tổng của 2 số Fibonacci trước đó là `fibonacci(n - 1)` và `fibonacci(n - 2)`.

*Lưu ý:* Phương pháp đệ quy thuần túy này có độ phức tạp thời gian là $O(2^n)$. Đối với $n$ lớn, bạn có thể áp dụng thêm **memoization** (`@functools.lru_cache`) để tối ưu hiệu năng.

Dưới đây là hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng:
n = 10
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n} là: {fibonacci(n)}")
```

### Giải thích:
- **Trường hợp cơ sở (Base case):** Nếu `n <= 0` trả về 0, nếu `n == 1` trả về 1.
- **Bước đệ quy (Recursive step):** Tính tổng của 2 số Fibonacci trước đó là `fibonacci(n - 1)` và `fibonacci(n - 2)`.

*Lưu ý:* Phương pháp đệ quy thuần túy này có độ phức tạp thời gian là $O(2^n)$. Đối với $n$ lớn, bạn có thể áp dụng thêm **memoization** (`@functools.lru_cache`) để tối ưu hiệu năng.
